q: Sharks swim in a huge body of salty water. What is it called?
why: The ocean is enormous and salty. Puddles and ponds are small, and sharks could not live in them.
hint: It covers most of our planet.

q: A map is a drawing that shows where places are.
why: Maps show where things are, like towns, roads, mountains and oceans.
hint: Think of what you use to find your way.

q: Which vehicle can carry people across the ocean?
why: Ships float on water and are big enough to carry many people far across the sea.
hint: Think about what floats.

q: A lifeguard sits by the beach. What is a lifeguard's job?
why: Lifeguards watch the water and help swimmers who are in trouble.
hint: The word says it: guarding lives.

q: A baseball ticket costs 4 dollars. How many dollars do 2 tickets cost?
why: Two tickets means 4 plus 4, which makes 8 dollars.
hint: Add the price two times.

q: Tacos are a famous food from which country?
why: Tacos come from Mexico, where cooks fill warm tortillas with tasty things.
hint: It is just south of the United States.

q: The Great Wall is a very long stone wall built on hills and mountains. Which country is it in?
why: The Great Wall of China winds across the northern part of the country for thousands of miles.
hint: The wall's full name includes the answer.

q: Put these steps in order for riding a bus to school.
why: You must wait for the bus before you can get on, ride it, and get off.
hint: What must happen before you can ride?

q: Which vehicle can travel underwater?
why: Submarines are built to dive and stay underwater. Helicopters fly and buses drive on roads.
hint: The word starts with a part meaning under.

q: Dinosaur bones that slowly turned into stone are called what?
why: Fossils form when buried bones turn to rock over millions of years. Some are 66 million years old.
hint: They come from long, long ago.

q: All the countries in the world share the same flag.
why: A flag is a symbol for a country. Each country has its own flag with its own colors and design.
hint: Think of flags at the Olympics.

q: What should drivers do at a red traffic light?
why: Red means stop. Waiting at red lights keeps drivers and walkers safe.
hint: Think of the colors of a traffic light.

q: Which vehicle carries astronauts up into space?
why: A rocket pushes very hard to climb above the air and carry astronauts into space.
hint: It blasts off with fire and smoke.

q: Put these bodies of water in order from smallest to biggest.
why: Puddles are tiny, ponds are bigger, and oceans are so big that whales and sharks roam them.
hint: Think about what could hold a whale.

q: You save 2 dollars every week. How many dollars will you have after 3 weeks?
why: Add 2 three times: 2 plus 2 plus 2 makes 6 dollars.
hint: Count by twos.

q: Which invention lets you talk with a friend who is far away?
why: A telephone carries voices over long distances. A compass shows direction and a ruler measures.
hint: You hold it near your ear.

q: "Hola" is a way to say hello in which language?
why: Hola is Spanish for hello. Spanish is spoken in Mexico, Spain and many other countries.
hint: Many people in Mexico say it.

q: A globe is a flat piece of paper.
why: A globe is a ball-shaped model of Earth. A flat piece of paper is a map.
hint: Think of a ball you could spin.

q: You drop coins into a jar and do not spend them. What are you doing?
why: Saving means keeping money to use later, like for a big toy or a trip.
hint: You are keeping it for later.

q: Every day the Sun comes up in the...
why: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west. It looks like it moves, but Earth is spinning.
hint: Sunset happens in the west.

q: The Amazon is one of the mightiest rivers on Earth. It flows through which continent?
why: The Amazon River winds through the rainforests of South America and empties into the Atlantic Ocean.
hint: Think of the rainforest next to the Andes.

q: A ship sails from Japan to California. Which ocean does it cross?
why: Japan is in Asia and California is in North America, and the Pacific Ocean lies between them. It is Earth's widest ocean.
hint: Both places touch the same huge ocean.

q: Some sharks live in the freezing cold Arctic Ocean.
why: Greenland sharks swim in icy Arctic water. Sharks are not only found in warm tropical seas.
hint: Think about whether sharks can handle cold.

q: What do we call money a worker is paid for doing a job?
why: Pay is money earned from working. A price tag shows what something costs, and a loan is borrowed money.
hint: Workers get this for their work.

q: Put these ways to travel in order from slowest to fastest.
why: Walking is the slowest. Bikes go faster than walkers, cars faster than bikes, and jets fastest of all.
hint: Think about how far each goes in an hour.

q: Mount Fuji, a famous snowy volcano, is in which country?
why: Mount Fuji rises near the coast of Japan, a country made of many islands in the Pacific Ocean.
hint: The country is a chain of islands in Asia.

q: People in Brazil mostly speak which language?
why: Brazil is the biggest country in South America, and its people speak Portuguese. Most neighbors speak Spanish.
hint: It is not the language of most neighbors.

q: Baseball is played only in the United States.
why: Baseball is loved in Japan, the Dominican Republic, Cuba and many other countries, and fans cheer for it all over the world.
hint: Think of baseball stars from other countries.

q: A person who draws maps for a living is called a...
why: Cartographers study the land and draw maps. Librarians care for books and plumbers fix pipes.
hint: Think of someone who studies land and draws charts.

q: A tall tower on the coast flashes a bright light at night to warn ships. What is it called?
why: Lighthouses show sailors where rocks and shores are, so ships stay safe in the dark.
hint: It stands on the shore and shines at night.

q: A pack of 6 baseball cards costs 3 dollars. How many dollars do 4 packs cost?
why: Four packs of 3 dollars each is 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3, which is 12 dollars.
hint: Add 3 four times.

q: Pasta and pizza are famous foods from which country?
why: Italy gave the world pizza and pasta, and cooks there still make them with tomatoes and cheese.
hint: Its shape on a map looks like a boot.

q: Dinosaur fossils have been found in Antarctica.
why: Antarctica was once warm and green. Scientists have dug up dinosaur bones there from long ago.
hint: Think about Antarctica long, long ago.

q: What does a bridge help travelers do?
opts: Cross over a river or valley
why: Bridges hold up roads and train tracks over rivers and deep gaps so people can cross.
hint: Think about what is below a bridge.

q: What carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years?
why: The Colorado River slowly wore away rock, making the canyon deeper and deeper over millions of years.
hint: Think about what water slowly does to rock.

q: A shark swims 3 kilometers every hour. How many kilometers does it swim in 4 hours?
why: Four hours of 3 kilometers each is 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3, which equals 12 kilometers.
hint: Add 3 four times.

q: In 1969, astronauts landed on a place beyond Earth and walked there. Where did they land?
why: The Moon is Earth's nearest neighbor in space, so it was the first place astronauts landed. The Sun is far too hot.
hint: It is the closest place to Earth in space.

q: Which of these helped people carry heavy loads more easily?
why: Wheels roll instead of drag, so carts and wagons move heavy things with much less pushing.
hint: It rolls.

q: Australia is both a country and a continent.
why: Australia is one country that covers a whole continent by itself. Most continents have many countries.
hint: It is not shared with other countries.

q: If you borrow a library book, what should you promise to do?
why: Libraries share books with everyone. Returning yours lets the next reader enjoy it too.
hint: Libraries lend books, not give them away.

q: On a map, what does the legend (also called the key) tell you?
opts: Which way is north on the map
Who drew the map and when
How far apart two places are
why: The legend explains symbols, like a tent for a campground. The compass rose shows direction and the scale shows distance.
hint: Look for a small box that explains the pictures.

q: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
why: The Indian Ocean touches Africa, Asia and Australia. The Atlantic is on Africa's other side and the Pacific is east of Australia.
hint: Its name sounds like a country in Asia.

q: Great white sharks are found off the coasts of California, South Africa and Australia.
why: Great whites live in cool and warm coastal waters around the world, including all three of these places.
hint: Great whites swim in many oceans.

q: Which of these is a service, not a good?
why: A service is work someone does for you. Goods are things you can hold, like bats, sandwiches and bicycles.
hint: You cannot carry it home in a bag.

q: Put these inventions in order from oldest to newest.
why: Wheels are thousands of years old. The printing press came in the 1400s, the airplane in 1903 and personal computers later.
hint: Which one is older than writing on paper?

q: People say "arigato" to mean thank you in which language?
why: Arigato means thank you in Japanese. Korean, Hindi and Italian each have their own words for thanks.
hint: It is spoken on islands in the Pacific.

q: Mount Everest, Earth's highest mountain above sea level, belongs to which mountain range?
why: Everest is part of the Himalayas, a giant chain of mountains in Asia. The Rocky Mountains and Alps are in other places.
hint: It is in Asia.

q: A tag on a shark sends a signal every 2 hours. How many signals does it send in one whole day?
why: A day has 24 hours. Splitting 24 hours into groups of 2 hours gives 12 signals.
hint: How many 2s fit into 24?

q: What is a port?
opts: A small boat used for fishing trips
A flag that flies on a ship's mast
A rope tying a boat to a dock
A harbor where ships load cargo
why: Ports are busy places where cargo is lifted on and off big ships, and where passengers can board.
hint: Think about where ships stop.

q: Every country in the world uses the same kind of money.
why: Countries have their own money, like dollars, pesos or yen. A few groups of countries share one.
hint: Think about money from different countries.

q: Who looks after a national park and helps keep visitors and animals safe?
why: Park rangers protect wild places, answer visitors' questions and help people who get lost.
hint: Think of who protects wild places.

q: Why are dinosaur fossils often found in dry, rocky badlands?
opts: Wind and rain uncover buried bones
Dinosaurs only lived in dry places
Dry air turns bones into stone faster
Sand dunes carried the bones there
why: Dinosaurs lived in many places. In badlands, wind and rain wear away rock and show bones that were buried.
hint: Think about what wears rocks away.

q: A train travels 60 miles each hour. How many miles does it go in 3 hours?
why: Add 60 three times: 60 plus 60 plus 60 equals 180 miles.
hint: Add 60 three times.

q: It is daytime in North America but nighttime in Asia. Why?
opts: The Moon blocks sunlight over Asia each day
Earth spins, lighting one side at a time
The Sun travels all the way around Earth
Asia is much farther away from the Sun
why: Earth is a spinning ball, so the Sun lights only half of it. As Earth turns, day and night move around.
hint: Think about what Earth does every 24 hours.

q: The Dominican Republic, home to many baseball stars, sits in which sea?
why: The Dominican Republic shares an island with Haiti in the warm Caribbean Sea, southeast of Florida.
hint: Think of warm islands near Florida.

q: Put these places in order from highest to lowest.
why: Mountains tower above hills, beaches sit at sea level, and the ocean floor lies far below the waves.
hint: Start with the place nearest the clouds.

q: Ancient Egyptians wrote using little pictures and symbols called...
why: Hieroglyphs were carved on temples and painted on papyrus. Cuneiform used wedge marks on clay in Mesopotamia.
hint: Think of picture writing carved on temple walls.

q: Around 1610, Galileo used a new invention to see moons circling Jupiter. What was it?
why: Telescopes make faraway things look closer. A microscope magnifies tiny things.
hint: It brings faraway things close.

q: Some countries, like Switzerland, have more than one official language.
why: Switzerland officially uses German, French, Italian and Romansh. Many countries have more than one language.
hint: Think of a country with many neighbors.

q: A farmer grows wheat for bread. The family that buys the bread is called a...
why: Producers make goods. Consumers buy and use them. The farmer is a producer and the family is a consumer.
hint: The family eats it.

q: Southwest is halfway between which two directions?
why: Southwest blends south and west. North and west make northwest, and south and east make southeast.
hint: Say the name in two parts.

q: A store lowers its coat prices in spring. Why?
opts: Coats cost more to make in spring
More shoppers want coats in spring
Stores can only sell coats in winter
why: When fewer people want something, sellers often cut the price to sell what is left. Warm weather lowers demand for coats.
hint: Think about who wants a coat on a warm day.

q: The Atlantic Ocean touches North America, South America, Europe and Africa.
why: The Atlantic stretches between the Americas on one side and Europe and Africa on the other.
hint: Picture the Atlantic in the middle of a world map.

q: Which city is the capital of Australia?
why: Canberra was planned as the capital. Sydney and Melbourne are bigger and better known, so many people guess them.
hint: It is not the city with the famous opera house.

q: A phone shows your spot on a map using GPS. GPS works by listening to signals from...
opts: Cables buried deep under the ground
Giant towers built on the Moon
why: GPS satellites orbit high above Earth and send signals. A phone uses them to work out exactly where it is.
hint: They travel far above the sky.

q: A ship sails 20 miles each hour. How many hours does it need to sail 100 miles?
why: Divide 100 miles by 20 miles per hour. Five hours of sailing covers 100 miles.
hint: How many 20s make 100?

q: The English word "safari" comes from Swahili, a language of East Africa. What does "safari" mean there?
why: Safari means journey in Swahili. The word came into English from people who made long trips across Africa.
hint: Many people go on one to see wild animals.

q: Which scientist studies weather and warns towns when a hurricane is coming?
why: Meteorologists study air and weather. Oceanographers study the sea, geologists study rocks and cartographers make maps.
hint: Think about the weather forecast.

q: Put these in order from earliest to most recent.
why: Dinosaurs came first by far. Cave art is tens of thousands of years old, pyramids are thousands, and the Moon landing was in 1969.
hint: Which happened before any people existed?

q: Passing through the Strait of Gibraltar takes ships between the Atlantic Ocean and which sea?
why: Gibraltar is a narrow gap between Spain and Morocco. It joins the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.
hint: The sea lies between Europe and Africa.

q: Chocolate is made from the beans of the cacao tree. Where did people first grow cacao?
opts: High, snowy mountain peaks of Asia
Dry, sandy deserts of North Africa
Cold, windy plains of northern Europe
why: Cacao trees need heat and rain. People in Central and South America used cacao long before Europe ever tasted chocolate.
hint: Cacao trees need heat and rain.

q: Big cities almost never grow up beside rivers or harbors.
why: Boats carried food and goods cheaply, so people settled by rivers and harbors. Many large cities grew from those spots.
hint: How did goods travel long ago?

q: A scientist attaches a small tag to a shark. What can the tag help show?
opts: How many teeth it will grow
why: Tags record a shark's path and how deep it dives. They cannot count teeth or show what it ate.
hint: Think about maps and travel.

q: The Gobi Desert is famous for dinosaur nests with eggs inside. On which continent is the Gobi?
why: The Gobi stretches across Mongolia and northern China. Fossil hunters there have found dinosaur bones and nests.
hint: Think of Mongolia and China.

q: A stand sells 40 hot dogs at a baseball game for 3 dollars each. How many dollars does it earn?
why: 40 times 3 equals 120. Money earned from selling is called income, and profit is what is left after costs.
hint: Think 4 tens times 3.

q: Goods that a country sells to other countries are called...
why: Exports leave a country to be sold elsewhere. Imports are goods that come in from other countries.
hint: Think of 'ex' as in 'exit'.

q: Houses in very hot, sunny places are often painted white. Why?
opts: White paint stops strong winds from blowing in
White is the cheapest paint color to buy
White paint keeps heavy rain from soaking in
White reflects sunlight and keeps rooms cool
why: Light colors bounce sunlight away instead of soaking it up, so white walls stay cooler than dark ones.
hint: Think about wearing a white shirt on a sunny day.

q: Put these ways of sharing messages in order from oldest to newest.
why: Cave drawings are the oldest. Printed books came in the 1400s, telephones in the 1870s and email in the 1970s.
hint: Which ones need electricity?

q: What did the printing press make possible?
why: Before printing presses, people copied books by hand. Printing made books cheaper, so more people could read.
hint: Think about how books were made before it.

q: The Panama Canal lets ships travel between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans without sailing around which continent?
why: The canal cuts across Panama, a narrow strip of land. Ships save thousands of miles by not rounding South America.
hint: Think about the shape of the Americas.

q: Why do countries trade with each other?
opts: Trade helps only the country that sells
Every country makes everything it needs
Money cannot be used inside one country
Each has goods the other lacks
why: Climate, land and skills differ, so countries swap what they have plenty of for goods they cannot easily make.
hint: Think about bananas in a cold country.

q: Greenland looks as big as Africa on many flat world maps, but Africa is far larger. Why?
opts: Greenland has grown since maps were drawn
Greenland's ice makes the land taller
Flat maps stretch shapes near the poles
why: Flattening a round Earth stretches places near the poles. Africa is really about 14 times bigger than Greenland.
hint: Think about flattening an orange peel.

q: If you cross the International Date Line going west, the calendar jumps back one day.
why: Sailing west across the Date Line, in the Pacific, jumps the calendar forward a day. Going east takes a day away.
hint: Which way does a new day start?

q: What do we call a narrow strip of land that joins two bigger lands, with water on both sides?
why: Panama is an isthmus. A peninsula has water on three sides, and an archipelago is a chain of islands.
hint: Panama is the famous example.

q: Besides goods, what else traveled along the Silk Road, a web of trade routes linking China to the Mediterranean?
why: Papermaking and other ideas spread along the Silk Road, carried by travelers along with silk and spices.
hint: Travelers also shared what they knew.

q: Put these ocean zones in order from the surface down to the deepest.
why: Sunlight fades with depth, from the bright top layer to the dim twilight zone, the dark midnight zone and the trenches.
hint: Sunlight can only reach the top.

q: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars finally read Egyptian hieroglyphs. Why?
opts: A pharaoh had already translated it long ago
The same message was carved in three scripts
It was a full dictionary carved in stone
It showed a picture for every hieroglyph
why: One script was Greek, which scholars could read. They matched it with the hieroglyphs to crack the code.
hint: One of the scripts was already known.

q: A baseball game starts at 9:00 AM Thursday in Tokyo. Los Angeles is about 16 to 17 hours behind Tokyo. What day is it in Los Angeles?
why: Going back 16 or 17 hours from 9:00 AM Thursday crosses midnight, landing in the afternoon of the day before.
hint: Going back that many hours crosses midnight.

q: The Mediterranean Sea touches Europe, Africa and Asia.
why: Southern Europe, northern Africa and western Asia all have shores on the Mediterranean.
hint: Think of Spain, Egypt and Turkey.

q: Which of these countries has no ocean coast at all?
why: Switzerland is landlocked, surrounded by other countries. Portugal, Japan and Chile all have long ocean coasts.
hint: Think of the Alps in the middle of Europe.

q: The same kinds of dinosaur fossils turn up in South America and Africa. What best explains this?
opts: Both lands have the same climate today
Fossil hunters carried bones between continents
Dinosaurs could swim across the Atlantic
why: Long ago the continents formed one big landmass, so dinosaurs could walk between lands that are now far apart.
hint: Look at how the coastlines fit together.

q: Earth is about 40,000 kilometers around the Equator. A jet flies 800 kilometers each hour. How many hours would it take to fly all the way around?
why: Divide 40,000 by 800 to get 50 hours, which is more than two full days of flying.
hint: Divide the distance by the speed.

q: Which of these is usually paid for with taxes?
opts: A soccer ball in a store
why: Taxes pay for shared services like libraries, roads and fire stations. Shops and restaurants get their money from customers.
hint: Think of services everyone in town shares.

q: Most goods that cross the ocean travel in standard metal containers. Why are standard sizes useful?
opts: They fit ships, trains and trucks alike
They keep goods cold on the voyage
They make the cargo weigh less
They help ships travel faster than planes
why: Identical boxes stack neatly and move from ship to train to truck without unpacking, saving time and money.
hint: Think about stacking identical blocks.

q: Put these steps in order to show how a fish gets from the sea to a dinner table.
opts: The boat unloads at the port
A truck carries it to a store
A family cooks it at home
why: Goods travel from producer to consumer: the fish is caught, landed at port, trucked to a store, then bought and cooked.
hint: Follow the fish from sea to plate.

q: Why do pilots listen to air traffic controllers on the ground?
opts: To learn how many passengers are aboard
To get the plane's gas at the airport
To hear which snacks are on board
why: Controllers watch the sky and tell pilots when to take off, land or change course, so planes never get too close.
hint: Think of a busy sky with many planes.

q: Many rocket launch sites are close to the ocean. What is one good reason?
opts: Ocean waves help push the rocket upward
Cool sea air makes every rocket lighter
Falling pieces land in water, not on towns
Rockets use salty ocean water as their fuel
why: Rockets drop used-up parts as they climb. Launching over the sea keeps those pieces away from people.
hint: Think about where leftover parts fall.

q: An island can belong to only one country, never to two.
why: Borneo holds three countries and Ireland holds two. An island's borders can cross it just like a continent's.
hint: Think about land borders on islands.

q: A tagged shark swims through the waters of many countries. What does this show about protecting sharks?
opts: Sharks are safe once they leave land
Rules matter only close to the shore
One country's rules can protect it everywhere
Countries must work together to protect them
why: Sharks ignore borders. A shark safe in one country's waters can be in danger in the next, so countries must cooperate.
hint: Sharks do not stop at borders.

q: Farmers in the Andes and in Asia cut flat steps into mountainsides. Why?
opts: To block cold wind from villages
To keep animals from climbing up
Flat steps hold soil and water
To make the mountain look taller
why: These steps are called terraces. They keep soil and water from washing downhill so crops can grow on steep slopes.
hint: Think about rain running down a slope.

q: Britain is far to the north, yet its winters are fairly mild. What helps most?
opts: Volcanoes heat the island all winter
It sits close to the Equator
A warm ocean current flows nearby
Hot deserts lie right next to it
why: The North Atlantic Drift carries warm water from the tropics toward Europe, softening winters.
hint: Think about the water touching its coast.

q: Over many years most prices slowly rise, so a dollar buys less than it used to. What is this called?
why: Inflation is a general rise in prices. Interest is money paid for borrowing or saving.
hint: Think of a balloon filling with air.

q: The deepest place in the ocean is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.
why: The Mariana Trench is nearly 11 kilometers deep, and Everest is about 9 kilometers tall. Everest would sink out of sight.
hint: Compare how far down with how far up.

q: A ship sits where the Equator meets the Prime Meridian, at 0 degrees latitude and 0 degrees longitude. Which ocean is it in?
why: That spot is in the Gulf of Guinea, off West Africa. A weather buoy floats there.
hint: Picture where the two lines cross on a world map.

q: Fossils of sea creatures have been found high in the Himalayas. What does this show?
opts: The ocean once rose higher than Everest
Seabed was pushed up into mountains
why: Colliding plates pushed old seafloor up into mountains. The ocean never rose that high.
hint: What could lift rock for millions of years?

q: A bank pays 10 percent interest each year on your whole balance. You deposit 100 dollars. After 2 years, with the interest added each year, how many dollars do you have?
why: Year one adds 10 dollars, making 110. Year two adds 10 percent of 110, which is 11, making 121.
hint: Find the total after year one first.

q: Spanish, French, Italian and Portuguese all grew out of which ancient language?
why: These languages grew from the Latin spoken across the Roman Empire, which is why many of their words look alike.
hint: The ancient Romans spoke it.

q: Which of these countries is crossed by the Equator, so it lies in both hemispheres?
why: The Equator crosses northern Brazil. Peru lies south of it, and Mexico and Argentina are far from it.
hint: Think of the country around the Amazon's mouth.

q: Put these loan steps in the correct order.
opts: You ask a bank for a loan
The bank lends you the money
You use it to buy what you need
You pay the bank back with interest
why: A loan works in this order: ask, receive, spend, then repay with a little extra called interest.
hint: You cannot spend money before you have it.

q: A Roman aqueduct slopes gently downward all the way to the city. Why?
opts: Wind turned wheels that moved it
Animals pulled the water in buckets
why: Romans had no pumps. A steady downhill slope let gravity move the water over many miles.
hint: Which way does water like to flow?

q: On a flat map, flights from Los Angeles to Tokyo curve northward. Why do pilots fly this way?
opts: On a round Earth, that path is shortest
Planes must always stay within sight of land
Mapmakers drew these routes the wrong way
Strong ocean currents steer the planes north
why: The shortest path between far-apart places on a ball bends when shown on a flat map. It's called a great circle.
hint: Think of a string stretched across a globe.

q: The Arctic is a continent surrounded by ocean, while Antarctica is an ocean surrounded by land.
why: It is the other way around. The Arctic Ocean has land around it, and Antarctica is a continent with ocean around it.
hint: Compare the two ends of Earth.

q: Which shark can swim far up rivers into fresh water?
why: Bull sharks can live in fresh water and have been found far up rivers. Most other sharks stay in salty seas.
hint: It can handle both fresh water and salty seas.

q: The Dead Sea is far saltier than the ocean. Why does salt build up there?
opts: Salt-making fish live in its waters
Underwater volcanoes keep adding more salt
Strong winds blow salt in from the ocean
Water evaporates but the salt stays behind
why: Rivers carry in a little salt, but water can only leave by evaporating. Over time the salt piles up.
hint: What is left when water dries up?

q: Pretend 1 dollar can be traded for 10 pesos. A baseball ticket costs 50 pesos. How many dollars is that?
why: Each 10 pesos equals 1 dollar, and 50 pesos holds five groups of 10. So the ticket costs 5 dollars.
hint: How many 10s fit in 50?

q: Some of the earliest writing, pressed into clay, was used mostly for what?
opts: Making maps of the night stars
Teaching young kids how to read
why: In Mesopotamia, scribes pressed wedge marks into clay to record grain, animals and trades. Stories and poems came later.
hint: Think about what early traders needed to remember.

q: Chile is very long and narrow from north to south. Why does it have deserts in the north and snowy lands in the south?
opts: The south is much closer to the Sun
The whole country sits on the Equator
Sea winds blow in the snow and sand
why: Chile runs through many latitudes, from warm northern deserts to cold southern lands near Antarctica.
hint: Think about how far apart its ends are.

q: Put the steps of a shark-tagging study in order.
opts: They map its path from signals
why: The shark must be caught before tagging, then released. Later, the tag's signals let scientists map where it swims.
hint: What must happen before attaching anything?

q: Many rockets launch toward the east from sites near the Equator. How does that help?
opts: Warm air makes rockets weigh less
Earth's spin gives them a speed boost
Equator skies never have clouds or storms
The Moon always sits in the east
why: Earth spins toward the east, fastest at the Equator, so an eastward launch starts with a free boost.
hint: Think about how fast the ground itself moves.

q: When two countries trade, one of them must always lose.
why: Both sides trade because each expects to get something it values more than what it gives up.
hint: Would anyone trade if they always lost?
